explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration that counts as a match. `jV` is the library's own definition: `pullback.map _ _ _ _ V.ι (𝟙 T) (𝟙 _) ..`. The lemma only computes its second component. The proof is `pullback.lift_snd _ _ _` (in `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Limits/Shapes/Pullback/HasPullback.lean`), which works because `pullback.map` is built from `pullback.lift`. That is Mathlib's basic lemma for the universal property of pullbacks, applied to a library definition. It is a generic structural fact, like an `ext` or `map_*` lemma, so it does not carry any mathematical content of Mathlib's own. The content here lies entirely in how `jV` is defined, so under the rules this is not a duplicate or a special case. I did not find any Mathlib lemma about this particular construction (the pullback of `V.ι ≫ c` along `t`, mapped into the pullback of `c` along `t`).
